preferences.showEquationsHelp: Show the equations behind the readouts.

energyBalance.warming: Warming: more energy in than out
energyBalance.cooling: Cooling: more energy out than in
energyBalance.distanceAxis: Distance from the star (AU, log scale)
energyBalance.explanation1: A planet absorbs starlight on the disc it shows the star, and radiates infrared from its whole surface. Its temperature rises or falls until the infrared going out equals the starlight coming in: that is its equilibrium temperature.
energyBalance.explanation2: The disc has a quarter of the area of the sphere, so a planet that spreads the heat around (it spins, or winds carry the heat) divides the absorbed starlight by 4. A planet that keeps one face to its star and moves no heat divides it by only 2, so its day side is hotter.
energyBalance.explanation3: Albedo is the fraction of starlight a planet reflects: fresh snow and bright clouds reflect a lot, dark rock very little.
energyBalance.explanation4: Compare the equilibrium temperature with the measured surface temperature. For airless Mercury and thin-aired Mars they agree; Earth is 33 K warmer and Venus about 500 K warmer. The Greenhouse screen explains the difference.

greenhouse.verdictVapour: Water would boil away as vapour.
greenhouse.verdictSupercritical: Too hot and dense: water is a supercritical fluid.
greenhouse.explanation1: Most sunlight passes through an atmosphere to the ground, but gases such as water vapour and CO₂ absorb the infrared the ground gives off. They re-emit part of it back down, so the surface must warm until enough infrared escapes from the cold upper layers to balance the sunlight.
greenhouse.explanation2: The greenhouse strength τ (infrared optical depth) measures how opaque the atmosphere is to infrared. With τ ≈ 0.85 this model gives Earth its 288 K; Venus needs τ ≈ 140.
greenhouse.explanation3: Warm is not enough for liquid water: the air must also press hard enough. Below the triple point (611 Pa, about 0.006 bar) water goes straight from ice to vapour. Mars sits right at that pressure.
greenhouse.explanation4: This is a teaching model: real greenhouse warming depends on which gases absorb at which wavelengths, on clouds, and on convection.
